title: Scaled palette labels overlap neighbouring tool buttons
evidence: At 1280×720 / 150% text, button remains 52px high while its child content is 69px; Poisoned Package child is350px wide inside284px button. At200%, child grows90px high/440px wide. Confirmed in panels_project/panel_probe_results.json and screenshots/15_build_200.png. Child HBox/VBox does not propagate minimum size to the Button and neither label wraps.
reproduction: Set Text Size to150% or200%, close Settings, open Build, inspect Hacks or Links.
impact: Names/costs collide and get clipped; the drawn text no longer corresponds cleanly to the hit targets.
recommendation: Make the tool row a container-sized button or propagate child minimum height; wrap or split name/cost within the available width.
acceptance: At100/125/150/200% every visible tool name and cost occupies its own row, with no sibling overlap or horizontal truncation; the complete row remains clickable and scrollable.

title: Tool hover details are written into an invisible inspector
evidence: _on_hover updates hover_tool and _update_info builds the detailed body, but _process shows sel_scroll only for selection or current_tool, not hover_tool. Probe hovering nest records its homage/cost in info_body while inspector_visible=false. Standard delayed tooltip is still present; the separate immediate detail preview is the broken part.
reproduction: With no armed tool or selection, open Build and hover Mirai Dropper; inspect info_body and sel_scroll visibility.
impact: The intended hover preview provides no visible help; players must wait for a tooltip or arm the tool.
recommendation: Provide a visible compact hover preview that does not hide the hovered palette, or remove dead hover-inspector state and improve the tooltip intentionally.
acceptance: Hover/focus any tool exposes its help without first arming it, and the palette remains available under the pointer.

title: Locked tools do not name the research needed to unlock them
evidence: Tool tooltip is name+homage+cost; disabled state is based solely on _is_unlocked. No required technology is displayed or linked. For example Poisoned Package is disabled although the corresponding technology is named Supply-Chain Attacks.
reproduction: Start a new game, hover locked Poisoned Package, then compare the Tech list.
impact: Players must infer a differently named technology before they can act.
recommendation: Add a readable Locked—requires <technology> line and a route to that research card; retain readable names and costs while locked.
acceptance: Each locked tool identifies the exact technology and prerequisite chain; a player can navigate to the relevant card in one action.

title: Build costs give no live affordability or resource shortfall
evidence: Palette cost labels are set once to _cost_str; _process refreshes unlock state only. An unlocked tool with insufficient Cash/Intel has the same palette presentation as an affordable one.
reproduction: Research Cloud Cryptojacking, leave Cash below60, and compare its palette row before and after accumulating the required Cash.
impact: Placement failures are discovered after arming and selecting a map location.
recommendation: Show affordable/shortfall state beside each cost, while allowing intentional preview even when a resource is missing.
acceptance: A missing resource is named with its deficit and updates as stock changes; research lock and resource shortage are visually/textually distinct.

title: Palette does not expose production and processor operating recipes
evidence: Tool rows contain name and initial build cost only; tooltip contains homage. Actual producer rates and CONV input/output/fuel data in main.gd:21–37 appear only after selection of an installed structure.
reproduction: Compare Mirai vsCloud Cryptojacker, or Intel Lab vsExploit Forge before constructing them.
impact: Players cannot evaluate expected yield or recurring fuel needs when making the build decision.
recommendation: Add a compact functional summary: output resource/rate for producers and input→output/rate plus fuel for processors, with coverage modifiers explicitly qualified.
acceptance: Before arming a tool its base output or conversion recipe and recurring fuel are available in readable text, independently of icon colour.

title: Tunnel options lack a comparable set of operating metrics
evidence: Links rows show build cost; tooltip uses qualitative homage such as small/cheap/silent or fast/loud. Numeric capacity, upkeep/tile, trace/s and distance loss are in main.gd:58–64 and are not provided together for comparison.
reproduction: Open Build→Links and compare DNS Tunnel, VPN Tunnel and Reverse Shell before arming.
impact: Players choose tunnels by flavour and discover the actual cost/capacity consequences after deployment.
recommendation: Provide an aligned comparison or consistent tooltip fields for capacity, upkeep, trace and distance loss.
acceptance: Each tunnel exposes the same units/fields; players can compare a cheap route, cooling route and high-capacity route without placing them.

title: The Proc category label does not explain what it contains
evidence: The visible subcategory labels are Hacks/Proc/Links and Proc has no tooltip or introductory label. Its contents are processors plus Proxy conversion.
reproduction: Open Build and look at the Proc subcategory as a first-time player.
impact: A central resource-conversion action is behind an unexplained abbreviation.
recommendation: Use a readable category name such as Processing and provide a brief category description, adapting layout at large text sizes.
acceptance: The category meaning is apparent from its visible label or immediate help; names remain fully readable at supported text scales.

title: Arming a tool removes the palette needed to choose the next tool
evidence: show_info becomes true whenever current_tool is nonempty and hides build_scroll/build_cat_row. To switch tools the player must re-enter Build (which clears current_tool) before selecting a different row.
reproduction: Arm Phishing Kit, then attempt to immediately choose DNS Tunnel from the left panel.
impact: A repeated build→connect sequence needs a navigation reset between actions.
recommendation: Keep a compact tool switcher or an explicit Back to tools action beside the armed-tool help.
acceptance: From an armed tool the next available tool can be selected directly, with the pending link/placement state cancelled consistently.

title: Custom palette buttons need explicit accessible names
evidence: _tool_entry creates a Button with empty text and places tool names in child Labels; no explicit accessibility name/description is set in this construction. The probe confirms every tool button_text is empty. This is a proposed accessibility hardening, not a claimed screen-reader runtime failure.
reproduction: Inspect a palette button's own label/accessibility metadata and test keyboard/screen-reader navigation on the supported platform.
impact: Accessible announcement of the custom row is dependent on engine child-text inference rather than an explicit contract.
recommendation: Assign the button an explicit accessible name and description containing its tool name, role, cost and lock reason, using the supported Godot accessibility API.
acceptance: The platform screen reader announces a unique name, cost and availability for each tool; child labels do not cause duplicate announcements.

title: Research cards do not identify the exact unlocked tool
evidence: _tech_row shows t.name and t.desc but never renders t.unlocks. Several labels differ from the palette names, for example Onion Routing→Onion Route and Exploit Development→Exploit Forge.
reproduction: Read a Tech card and locate the tool it will enable in Build.
impact: Players cannot reliably connect research investment to a concrete action or build category.
recommendation: Render Unlocks: <tool name> with the matching glyph/category and optionally a jump action.
acceptance: Every technology lists the exact current palette names it unlocks before purchase and after it is researched.

title: HTTP/2's required technology is clipped even at default text size
evidence: At100% the Locked—needs Exploit Development button text measures345px inside a260px-wide button; clip_text is true and tooltip_text is empty. Probe panel_probe_results.json research[http2] captures width/text.
reproduction: Start a new game, open Tech, scroll to HTTP/2 Flooding and read its disabled button.
impact: The prerequisite name is truncated and has no alternate complete tooltip or separate label.
recommendation: Put the prerequisite in a wrapping card label and keep the disabled button short; expose the full reason through accessible help.
acceptance: Exploit Development is fully readable at100/125/150/200% without horizontal clipping or reliance on guesswork.

title: A prerequisite-locked research card hides its Research cost
evidence: For a not-ready technology _process replaces the entire button with Locked—needs <name>. The cost is only rendered in the ready branch, and _tech_row has no separate cost label. HTTP/2 costs25RP but that amount is hidden before Exploit Development.
reproduction: Before researching Exploit Development, inspect HTTP/2 Flooding and plan total Research needed for the two-step path.
impact: Players cannot budget the next unlock chain from the Tech panel.
recommendation: Display cost independently of the current action state, together with prerequisite requirements.
acceptance: A locked, affordable, unaffordable or completed technology consistently exposes its defined cost; the Exploits→HTTP/2 path can be budgeted before either purchase.

title: Disabled research purchases lack a local balance and shortfall
evidence: When prerequisites are satisfied b.disabled depends on resources.research<t.cost, while text remains Research (<cost>RP). No local current balance, remaining amount or tooltip is set.
reproduction: Open Tech with0RP, then with9RP, and compare an eligible10RP card.
impact: The player gets a disabled control without a clear local explanation of how close the unlock is.
recommendation: Add Research <current>/<required> and Need <deficit> messaging, plus a direct explanation of earning Research when the balance is zero.
acceptance: At9/10RP a10RP card states1RP missing; at10RP it becomes actionable immediately, and prerequisite lock remains a distinct status.

title: Research list keeps completed and unavailable cards ahead of actionable ones
evidence: Tech rows are created once in TECH dictionary insertion order and all remain visible; _process updates button text/state but provides no filter or prioritization.
reproduction: Research several early entries, then revisit Tech at200% text to locate remaining affordable research lower in the list.
impact: Repeated scrolling through already-completed cards slows progression planning.
recommendation: Offer stable Available/All/Researched filters or group actionable and completed technologies while preserving keyboard focus.
acceptance: Remaining eligible technologies can be viewed without scrolling through completed cards, and the full dependency/cost history remains accessible.

title: Contract board rebuild destroys keyboard focus after accepting a job
evidence: _rebuild_jobs queue_frees every existing child whenever _contracts_ver changes. In the probe an Accept button had focus; main.accept_contract triggered a rebuild, old card became invalid and gui_get_focus_owner became null.
reproduction: Keyboard-focus an Accept button, activate it and continue navigating the board. Also observe focus when a different contract completes.
impact: Keyboard navigation loses its position because all cards are replaced for a single state change.
recommendation: Update cards by contract ID or restore focus to the corresponding surviving card/action after rebuild.
acceptance: Accept, completion, claim and arrival preserve a meaningful focus target; an unrelated card changing state never clears the currently focused card.

title: Linked-structure contract text omits which nodes qualify
evidence: Jobs displays c.desc verbatim as Add N linked structures (main.gd:1947), but _contract_raw main.gd:1965 excludes the hub and every node with relay=true. A linked Proxy or a producer converted to Proxy therefore does not count, despite being a linked structure.
reproduction: Accept an Add N linked structures job and link/convert a Proxy; compare its connected state to the unchanged job progress.
impact: The literal objective promises progress for a central network structure that the evaluator excludes.
recommendation: Name the qualifying set explicitly, for example Add N linked producers/processors (Proxies excluded), or align the evaluator with the intended broad objective.
acceptance: The objective describes exactly the node categories counted; converting an eligible node explains any progress reduction.

title: Completed contracts have no notification outside the Jobs tab
evidence: The Jobs tab label is static; completion feedback exists only in card status/Claim button. main.gd:1988–1990 marks done and changes version without setting message. Probe completion retained message='baseline' even though done=true.
reproduction: Accept a job, switch to Build/Tech, meet the objective and observe the navigation/status UI.
impact: Earned rewards can remain undiscovered and occupy contract slots while the player works elsewhere.
recommendation: Add a claimable-count badge and a concise completion event with a direct jump to the completed card.
acceptance: Completion is signalled from any tab once per job; the badge remains until reward claim and opens the relevant claim action.

title: Accepted-job countdown shows zero before the deadline expires
evidence: The UI casts remaining deadline to int, flooring any positive fraction below1 to0. The evaluator expires only when deadline<=0, so a still-active job displays0s left.
reproduction: Observe an accepted contract when deadline is between0 and1 seconds.
impact: The timer reports expiry early and makes a last-second completion look inconsistent.
recommendation: Use ceil for a remaining-seconds countdown, or show a sub-second format near expiry.
acceptance: Every positive remaining deadline displays at least1s in the integer countdown;0/expired is reserved for actual expiry.

title: Contract deadline has no urgency state
evidence: All status labels receive the same green font colour at creation; _process updates text without changing appearance as a deadline approaches. There is no imminent-expiry cue beyond the decreasing number.
reproduction: Compare an accepted card with90 seconds remaining to the same card with5 seconds remaining.
impact: A time-critical task looks like ordinary healthy status and is easy to miss while managing the network.
recommendation: Introduce readable soon/urgent deadline states with text or an icon as well as colour, respecting reduced-motion settings.
acceptance: Near-expiry thresholds are evident without relying solely on colour or animation; completed/unaccepted cards are not marked urgent.

title: Claimable and active jobs can be hidden below unopened offers
evidence: _rebuild_jobs iterates main.contracts in arrival order. Three cards are supported, but claimable/urgent state does not alter ordering or provide a view filter; at200% only a fraction of the first card is visible in screenshot17_jobs_200.png.
reproduction: Keep the first offer unaccepted, accept the third, complete it, then revisit Jobs at large text size.
impact: The most actionable work requires scrolling past untouched offers, compounding the absence of external completion feedback.
recommendation: Offer Claimable/Active/Offers grouping or a pinned claimable summary while preserving stable card focus and IDs.
acceptance: Claimable rewards and active deadlines are discoverable before unopened offers; changing state does not unexpectedly move keyboard focus.
